items.subject: Isolate diagonal handling from per-interaction arithmetic changes
items.objective: Use the existing one-output-per-thread global traversal to test distinct inner-loop hypotheses. First compare the original diagonal skip with split ranges j<i and j>i, keeping the original force arithmetic; separately test acceleration accumulation and rsqrtf-based inverse-distance powers. Measure these individually before trying combinations. Preserve the specified softening, update order, exact masses, and finite outputs; check arbitrary sizes, coincident positions, zero/negative dt, and the isolated extreme-mass case. items.subject: Measure shared-memory staging against cached global reads
items.objective: Test CTA-level source staging with one target per thread, keeping the original interaction arithmetic as a control. Compare global traversal and shared-memory staging at matched block configuration; stage only x, y, z, and mass as a compact alternative to staging full Particle records. Since source-load reuse may already be served by the hardware cache, treat benefit as a hypothesis. Tune within the shared-memory limit, handle source and target tails, and ensure every thread reaches required barriers. Write only the permitted kernel and launch files; validate and time with the official protocol. Combinations with other ideas remain available after isolated tests.

items.subject: Separate launch-geometry tuning from register-blocked target reuse
items.objective: Keep global-memory traversal and baseline pair arithmetic as controls. First measure one-output-per-thread launch configurations with items_per_block equal to block; then test bounded per-thread target batches, reusing each source record across the batch. This separates launch-geometry effects from register-level reuse. Respect the required grid formula, bound register use, and handle arbitrary sizes and partial batches without specializing to benchmark sizes. Write only the permitted kernel and launch files; validate and time with the official protocol. Further correctness-preserving combinations are not excluded.
